caveat: Mobilize Financial Services earned 2,224m euro of net banking income on 59.3bn euro of average performing assets in 2025, or 3.75%. On this car's contract - 85% of list amortising to zero over 48 months, so an average outstanding of about 5,300 euro - that is 797 euro over four years. The group-level figure must exclude rate support paid by the new-car business to the finance arm, which is an internal transfer: the high bound removes none of it, the low bound removes half.

label: Per-car P&L - credit losses over the contract
source: Our estimate, from published European captive cost of risk
caveat: Mobilize Financial Services' cost of risk was 0.31% of average performing assets in 2024 and 0.30% in 2023; Volkswagen Financial Services' net loss ratio has run below 0.5%. Applied to the same average outstanding of about 5,300 euro over four years, 0.31% gives 66 euro and 0.5% gives 106 euro. A cost-of-risk figure is cyclical and these are benign years.

label: Per-car P&L - service and parts margin over the contract
source: Our estimate; no source divides aftersales profit by cars on the road
caveat: Vertu Motors, a UK franchised retailer, earned a 44.4% gross margin on aftersales in the year to February 2026 - 73.4% on service labour, 20.9% on parts - and aftersales produced over 46% of its gross profit. The group captures the parts margin on a car it built, and the service margin only where it owns the network. No published source divides aftersales profit by vehicles in operation, so the euro amount per car is our judgement and the range is wide.

label: Per-car P&L - reconditioning, logistics and holding
source: Our estimate, against published reconditioning costs
caveat: Average reconditioning is reported at about 1,112 dollars a vehicle and dealer reconditioning fees at 500 to 2,000 dollars - US consumer-guide figures, not audited accounts. A small hatchback coming off a maintained lease should cost less than an average trade-in, which is why the central figure sits below the US average. Holding cost is real too: cap hpi puts depreciation on a used family hatchback at about 7 pounds a day while it waits to be listed.

label: Per-car P&L - remarketing margin
source: Our estimate, against an independent retailer's used margin
caveat: Vertu Motors made 1,501 pounds of gross profit on each of 91,287 used vehicles in the year to February 2026, about 1,725 euro, and that is after its own preparation charges. An independent retailer captures the whole trade-to-retail spread; the group buying its own car back at a contractual residual has already passed that value to the customer, so its used side earns far less. With reconditioning taken out separately, the central figures leave the used side at about -200 euro a car.

label: Programme cost - platform, data and licences
caveat: Ledger platform, entity-resolution and data acquisition, and licences over two years. The same in all four X25 build scenarios; with inv_change_eur_m, nearly half of an in-house build, and the part X25 did not price from a source. No vendor quotation has been taken (X25 has list prices for parts of it: senzing_*, sf_auto_*). Benchmark (X14): Ayvens spent EUR 525m over 2022-2025 to integrate LeasePlan for EUR 440m a year of synergies (ayvens_*), a whole merger with core IT migrations; this programme is a data layer on existing systems, so the figure is a scale reference, not a like-for-like benchmark. None was found.

Benchmark (X14): Ayvens spent EUR 525m over 2022-2025 to integrate LeasePlan for EUR 440m a year of synergies (ayvens_*), a whole merger with core IT migrations; this programme is a data layer on existing systems, so the figure is a scale reference, not a like-for-like benchmark. label: Phase 1 gate - incentive spend linked to a VIN
caveat: The programme's first job is to see the spend. Below this the incentive-to-resale link cannot be measured on the bulk of it, so Phase 2 would have nothing to learn from. Measured on claim value rather than claim count, so a few large claims cannot be quietly left out. If missed: Delay (X22): the next phase's funding waits while the build continues on Phase 1's money. A count over every claim, readable in the phase.

label: Phase 1 gate - dealer code crosswalk coverage
caveat: Set level with the VIN link, because a claim can only be de-duplicated once both the car and the dealer resolve to one identity. The two together are what makes a duplicate provable. If missed: Delay (X22), as gate_vin_link_pct.

label: Phase 1 gate - duplicate flags that are real
caveat: A false duplicate withholds an honest dealer's money, so precision is gated harder than recall. Measured on used-car adverts, an exact rule scored 98.7% precision and a relaxed one 20.7% (er_exact_precision, er_relax_precision), so 90% is where a scored match with a review band is working rather than either extreme. Those rates do not transfer to claims data. Read (X22) on an audit of flagged claims: the exact one-sided lower bound must clear this level at gate_read_confidence_pct, on a sample sized in advance (x22_audit_n_prec95). If missed: Waiver with re-review, flags go to human review rather than to hold until it reads.

label: Phase 1 gate - real duplicates that get flagged
caveat: Missing a duplicate costs money once; wrongly flagging one costs a dealer relationship, so recall is set below precision and the rest is caught in the human review band. The measured design clears it with room: automatic linking above the upper threshold caught 80.3% and the worked review band 96.0% (er_auto_link_recall, er_review_band_recall). Read (X22) on duplicates seeded into the claims stream with known answers (X1's method), since a random audit could not find enough rare real ones; the sample is sized in advance (x22_seed_n_rec80). If missed: Waiver with re-review.

label: Phase 2 gate - ledger against the general ledger
caveat: Finance will not certify a benefit out of a ledger it cannot tie to the books. This is the gate that makes every later euro figure arguable in a committee rather than only in a model. If missed: Delay (X22); read at every monthly close.

label: Phase 2 gate - retention uplift over a randomised control group
caveat: Deliberately set below the 3pp the value-at-risk model assumes (upgrade_capture_uplift, range 1-6pp), so the pilot can come in under the assumption and still pass, and so that failing the gate is a real possibility rather than a formality. Testable: randomising the group's own flag within each dealer needs x15_pilot_blocked_customers per arm (analysis/pilot_size_report.md). Read (X22) on orders signed inside Phase 2 by customers whose contracts end in its first half, the group's flag randomised within dealers (X15), one pre-registered arm and one O'Brien-Fleming interim look; the point estimate must reach this level and the lower bound clear zero. The lower bound, not the point estimate, then replaces upgrade_capture_uplift in the benefits case (x22_lower_at_gate_pp; a significant result overstates the effect, gc_exaggeration_80_power). If missed: Back-up, cohort-level timing and the exit gate's fallback line.

label: Phase 2 gate - confidence required on that uplift
caveat: A randomised control group is the only thing that turns the assumed euros of leak 2 into a measured number, so the standard is the conventional one and the holdout must be preserved.

label: Phase 4 exit - run-rate benefits certified by Finance
source: Team choice, derived on the Benefits sheet (X21)
caveat: Derived, not chosen: the run rate the committed levers (claims controls, retention, resale execution) earn in the markets live at month 24, at the reference class (McKinsey-Oxford's software projects fall short of their benefits, mckox_sw_benefit_shortfall_pct), with every source; rounded. On the named fallback without the joint ventures' data, the gate is the Benefits sheet's second line. Finance certifies it against control groups. It replaces a gate set above an older controls figure and at about four times the old single ask (retired by X25), true by construction (skeptic B1); the old gate was above what the plan itself earns in those markets. The floor beneath it on the Benefits sheet is X22's stop. The audit checks this row against the sheet. Outcomes (X22): Go (roll out) at or above it; Waiver with re-review between it and the floor (gate_exit_floor_s1..s4_eur_m, one per build scenario): stay in the live markets; Kill below the floor, with no run cost committed.

label: KPI - days to settle an incentive claim
caveat: A controls layer that holds claims for review only works if the review is fast; a slow one gets overridden by the business and the control stops existing.

label: KPI - record pairs sent to human review
caveat: A capacity limit, not an accuracy one: it is what a review team can actually work. The measured threshold sweep put 8,344 pairs in the band on used-car adverts (er_review_band_pairs), which is what sizing this on real claims would look like.

label: KPI - market drift carried unseen between re-marks
caveat: Sits between the two measured cadences: 3.0% of level can drift unseen at today's quarterly review and 1.3% at monthly (level_3m_p5, level_1m_p5). Set between them so the target is reachable but not free, and so it is an exposure measure rather than a claimed saving.

label: KPI - error on little-history cars against established markets
caveat: New brands, new markets and electrified lines are where borrowing data pays; the measured gain is 4.3% at 100 local cars and nothing by 250 (pooling_gain_100, pooling_gain_250), so the target is closing a gap, not reaching parity.

label: Design choice - average band within which a pricer may adjust the recommendation, tied to the engine's calibrated band (X13)
source: Design choice, from adoption research and X13 (26 September)
caveat: People use an imperfect algorithm far more when they can modify its output even slightly, and the band's width barely changes that (Dietvorst, Simmons & Massey 2018; x13_dv_uptake_*). Since X13 the band is tied to the value engine's calibrated 80% band and scaled to this average, so it is narrower on young cars and wider on old ones (x13_tied_cap_*). In X13's model it is never worse than a flat ±5% at any level of pricer information (x13_be_tied_vs_fixed). The full calibrated band pays only if pricers see enough of the engine's error (x13_be_full_vs_fixed*), which the pilot measures before any widening. The average stays small because the level, not the pricer, is what moves value.

caveat: Sum of lags 0 to 48 months, 32 European markets, country and month fixed effects, standard errors clustered by country. Nothing. An index mixing every vintage also dilutes one cohort's discount about tenfold, so this test has little power even in principle.

label: Eurostat - the same moves showing up in used prices beforehand
anchor: Everything before it adds to
caveat: Larger than everything that comes after, so used prices move ahead of new-car prices. The Tesla failure is general, not a quirk of one January. A market-level series cannot answer this question; the per-car link can.

label: Published - resale value lost at 36 months per 10% discount at the new sale
source: Holweg M. and Kattuman P., 'A dynamic determination of the residual product value: empirical evidence from the automotive industry', POMS conference paper 004-0144, Table 5 and section 4.3
caveat: UK auction (trade) prices from Glass's CAP, 1999-2004, 2,320 model-months, 47-48 models, 70.22% of UK registrations. A conference paper; no journal version found, and the paper never names the source of its discount variable. Model fixed effects, year and month effects and macro controls, but not a causal design - a model that needs discounting may be a weak model anyway, though age-of-design and new-model dummies absorb the main lifecycle channel. Table 5 coefficient -0.00647 per percentage point, t 8.24.

source: Holweg M. and Kattuman P., 'A dynamic determination of the residual product value: empirical evidence from the automotive industry', POMS conference paper 004-0144, Table 5 and section 4.3
caveat: UK auction (trade) prices from Glass's CAP, 1999-2004, 2,320 model-months, 47-48 models, 70.22% of UK registrations. Model fixed effects, year and month effects and macro controls, but not a causal design - a model that needs discounting may be a weak model anyway, though age-of-design and new-model dummies absorb the main lifecycle channel. label: Reading data stored in a user's terminal equipment needs consent, unless strictly necessary for a service the user asked for
source: Directive 2002/58/EC as amended by 2009/136/EC, Art 5(3): "only allowed on condition that the subscriber or user concerned has given his or her consent"
caveat: With edpb_connected_vehicle_terminal: reading a car's data needs the user's consent or a service the user requested (X20).

label: EDPB: a connected vehicle is terminal equipment, so ePrivacy Art 5(3) applies
source: EDPB Guidelines 01/2020 on processing personal data in the context of connected vehicles and mobility related applications, v2.0 (adopted 9 March 2021), para 13: "the connected vehicle and device connected to it should be considered as a 'terminal equipment' (just like a computer, a smartphone or a smart TV) and provisions of art. 5(3) ePrivacy directive apply where relevant"
caveat: Guidance, not law. The ledger reads odometer and battery at a car's return under the user's contract or consent (X20).

label: EDPB: pseudonymised data remain personal data even when the key is held by another party
source: EDPB Guidelines 01/2025 on Pseudonymisation: pseudonymised data "is to be considered information on an identifiable natural person ... This statement also holds true if pseudonymised data and additional information are not in the hands of the same person"; the risk reduction "may enable controllers to rely on legitimate interests under Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR"
caveat: Adopted for consultation January 2025. Backs X1's design rule (the customer link held apart) and keyed matching with a joint venture; a hashed VIN is still personal data (X20).

label: GDPR: processing strictly necessary to prevent fraud is a legitimate interest
source: Regulation (EU) 2016/679, Recital 47: "The processing of personal data strictly necessary for the purposes of preventing fraud also constitutes a legitimate interest of the data controller concerned"
caveat: The basis for checking a dealer's incentive claim against independent sources (Art 6(1)(f)); still needs a balancing test (X20).

label: GDPR: joint controllers must set their responsibilities in an arrangement
source: Regulation (EU) 2016/679, Art 26(1): "Where two or more controllers jointly determine the purposes and means of processing, they shall be joint controllers. They shall in a transparent manner determine their respective responsibilities ... by means of an arrangement between them"
caveat: A shared upgrade programme with a joint venture (the group's timing, the partner's contact) needs one (X20).

label: Data Act: connected products must make their data accessible to the user by design, for products placed on the market after 12 September 2026
source: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854, Art 3(1) and Art 50: "The obligation resulting from Article 3(1) shall apply to connected products and the services related to them placed on the market after 12 September 2026"
caveat: Cars sold before then have no design duty; the rest of the Act applies from 12 September 2025 (data_act_rules).

label: Data Act: the owner and anyone with contracted rights to use the car (a lessee or renter) are users
source: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854, Art 2(12): "'user' means a natural or legal person that owns a connected product or to whom temporary rights to use that connected product have been contractually transferred"; Art 4(13): the data holder uses non-personal data "on the basis of a contract with the user"
caveat: So a leasing company or rental firm is a user of the cars it holds: a data clause in the group's own lease and buy-back contracts is a route to returned cars' data. A private driver's personal data still needs a GDPR basis (X20).

caveat: VIN-level proof of sale for an incentive claim implements the incentive programme; dealers' transaction prices must not be used to steer resale prices (vber_art4a_rpm) (X20).
